mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday situations best demonstrates the concept of inertia?

options.A: A ball rolling down a slope speeds up.
options.B: A passenger lurches forward when a bus suddenly stops.
options.C: A kite flies higher when wind speed increases.

mcqs.answer: A passenger lurches forward when a bus suddenly stops.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the resistance to change in motion. When the bus stops abruptly, the passenger tends to continue moving forward, illustrating inertia. Option A shows acceleration, not inertia. Option C involves external force (wind). Option D is about magnetic attraction, not inertia.

mcqs.question: A book is lying undisturbed on a table. Which statement correctly defines inertia in this situation?

options.A: Inertia is the force that keeps the book moving.
options.B: Inertia is the tendency of the book to stay at rest unless a force acts on it.
options.C: Inertia is the speed of the book.
options.D: Inertia is the weight of the book.

mcqs.answer: Inertia is the tendency of the book to stay at rest unless a force acts on it.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia refers to an object's natural tendency to maintain its current state of motion, whether at rest or moving uniformly. The book remains at rest because of its inertia; a force is needed to change that. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated concepts (force, speed, weight).

mcqs.question: Many think that an object at rest has no inertia. Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Objects at rest have zero inertia.
options.B: Inertia only exists when objects are moving.
options.C: Even when at rest, an object possesses inertia equal to its mass.
options.D: Inertia depends on shape, not mass.

mcqs.answer: Even when at rest, an object possesses inertia equal to its mass.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is a property of mass; it exists whether the object is moving or stationary. Therefore, a stationary object still has inertia proportional to its mass. Options A and B deny inertia at rest, which is incorrect. Option D confuses inertia with shape-dependent factors like drag.

mcqs.question: A hockey puck slides on ice and continues moving for a long distance. Which reasoning best explains this observation?

options.A: The puck is constantly pushed by the ice.
options.B: The puck has low inertia, so it stops quickly.
options.C: The puck’s inertia keeps it moving in the same direction unless acted upon by friction.
options.D: The puck’s mass increases as it moves.

mcqs.answer: The puck’s inertia keeps it moving in the same direction unless acted upon by friction.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia causes the puck to maintain its state of uniform motion. On ice, friction is minimal, so the puck keeps moving. Option A incorrectly suggests a continuous force. Option B misstates inertia (low inertia would mean it stops easily). Option D is physically impossible.

mcqs.question: How does inertia of direction differ from inertia of speed?

options.A: Inertia of direction resists change in speed, while inertia of speed resists change in direction.
options.B: Inertia of direction resists change in the line of motion, while inertia of speed resists change in magnitude of velocity.
options.C: Both are the same; there is no difference.
options.D: Inertia of direction applies only to rotating bodies.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of direction resists change in the line of motion, while inertia of speed resists change in magnitude of velocity.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction (or path) opposes a change in the direction of motion, whereas inertia of speed (or magnitude) opposes a change in how fast the object moves. Option A swaps the definitions. Option C ignores the distinction. Option D incorrectly limits direction inertia to rotation.

mcqs.question: In which of the following safety devices does the principle of inertia play a crucial role?

options.B: The colour of a house’s paint
options.D: The type of music played in a store

mcqs.explanation: Seat belts restrain occupants, using inertia: when a car stops suddenly, the occupants tend to continue moving forward due to inertia; the belt provides the external force needed to change that motion safely. Options B, C, and D are unrelated to inertia.

mcqs.question: Inertia is best defined as:

options.A: The tendency of an object to change its state of motion.
options.B: The tendency of an object to remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
options.C: The force required to start moving an object.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of an object to remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: This definition captures Newton’s first law. Option A states the opposite (change). Option C describes force, not inertia. Option D describes speed, not inertia.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes inertia of rest?

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest unless a net external force acts on it.
options.B: An object at rest will start moving on its own.
options.C: Inertia of rest means objects cannot be moved.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest will stay at rest unless a net external force acts on it.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means a stationary object resists any change in its state; it remains stationary until a force acts. Option B contradicts inertia. Option C exaggerates inertia, implying immovability. Option D confuses mass with inertia.
